title: Sensor Calibration Record Test Sheet
source: spec/Sensor_Calibration_Record_Test_Sheet.html — a one-page sheet: client band, "Type of Sensor" bar, one add/delete-row data table, two free-text boxes, and a three-row sign-off. The supplied file was saved with a completed record in it (AMK3 Level 6 Network RM, room temperature / humidity / TA smart valve); those are record values, not template values, and are not carried here.

sections.title: Record Test Data
sections._note:
"Type of Sensor" is carried as a header field, not a section: it is the source's own bar between the title and this table, one sheet covers one sensor type, and every row inherits it — a section of its own would also cost the page a heading and a block it cannot spare.

`page_break_before` on the opening section is what keeps this on one sheet: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same idiom as `fcu-lcp-checklist.json`. min_rows matches the source's three seeded rows; the source adds and deletes rows freely, which is what `dynamic_table` gives.

**Every measurement column is `text`, not `number`.** The source writes the unit into the cell alongside the figure — "22.8 °C", "76.0%", "0.25 L/s" in the sample — because one sheet is used for temperature, humidity and flow sensors and the unit follows the sensor type, which is chosen per record. A `number` column would need a fixed `unit` in the template and would reject the readings this form is designed to take.

Offset is recorded, not derived: it is Field − BMS on a temperature row, but the source leaves it typed and a sheet may carry non-numeric readings, so `lib/formula.ts` is not wired here.

sections.title: Test Instrument / Tools Required
sections._note: The source heads this a free-text box. A table instead, as on `ahu-supply-fresh-air-measurement.json` §9: only a table can be read by `link_to_instrument_register` (SPEC §5). That matters more here than on any other sheet in the library — this record calibrates a sensor AGAINST a reference instrument, so an out-of-calibration reference invalidates every row above it.

sections.title: Remarks
sections._note: A `field_group`, as on `condensate-pipe-flood-test.json`, not the `standard` + textarea-row shape used by the AHU/FCU air measurement templates. A standard section always prints its serial and remarks columns, so a lone textarea row came out as an empty serial column, a Description column carrying the prompt, and TWO columns both headed Remarks. The source is a plain labelled box; this prints as one.

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note:
An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, which would print a one-page source on two sheets. Both routes carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. Same idiom as `ductwork-air-leakage-test.json`.

The source has THREE rows and heads the lower two identically, "Witnessed By" — the roles read the same on the paper and are kept that way; the distinct `stage` values are what drive the workflow (SPEC §6), as on `ductwork-air-leakage-test.json`.
